title: LOBSTER principal terminology ledger

home.mirror: sim/worker-kit (verbatim copy of the whole directory; see USAGE.md "Two branches, one ledger")

seededBy: cloud coordinator session, from the 2026-08-26..28 transcript
readMe: WHAT THIS IS. A per-principal record of which project vocabulary each human
has actually been given. It exists because the coordinator repeatedly briefed
the owner in codebase jargon he had never been handed, and he said so:
"you really suck at empathizing with what I already understand" (2026-08-28).
THE ONE RULE. Never use a term in an owner briefing unless the ledger says it
is `native` (they used it correctly themselves) or `defined` (we formally
defined it, on a date, somewhere). Anything `internal` or `corrected` must be
defined inline at first use -- and the definition recorded here in the SAME
work cycle, or the ledger is already lying.
EVIDENCE OR IT DID NOT HAPPEN. Every state carries at least one evidence entry
with a date. `native` and `corrected` need a quote fragment from the principal.
A familiarity claim gets the same epistemic hygiene as an experimental claim.

states.native: The principal used the term correctly themselves. Strongest evidence. Safe to use unqualified.
states.defined: Formally defined for the principal in a dedicated briefing, with a date and a location. Safe to use; a one-clause reminder is still courteous.
states.corrected: The principal explicitly flagged the term as unfamiliar. MUST be re-defined at every use, even if previously `defined`. Corrections never auto-expire.
states.internal: Lives in code or agent reports and has NEVER been briefed. Must be defined inline at first use, or avoided in favour of a native synonym.

notes: The stoplist is append-as-you-go. Adding a token here is a claim that it is
ordinary English or a proper noun -- NOT a way to silence real jargon. If it
is project vocabulary, give it a ledger entry instead.

notes.quote: you've just given me explanations for a bunch of your lingo without actually connecting to your lingo
notes.lesson: A glossary dump is not a definition. Define a term where it is USED, in the sentence that uses it.

notes.quote: I don't understand your 'what needs you' entries at all
notes.lesson: Section headings and status labels are terminology too. Internal report structure is jargon.

notes.quote: you really suck at empathizing with what I already understand
notes.lesson: The founding mandate for this ledger. Familiarity is not to be assumed; it is to be tracked, with evidence, and deduced by elimination.

notes.quote: design a dedicated memory system within repos for you to track across sessions which terminology each human principal involved in a project is so far familiar with
notes.lesson: This file is that system. It lives in the repo so every session -- cloud coordinator, local sim worker, post-compaction resume -- reads the same state.

notes.quote: holy shit! I did not say this and this is exactly the mistake I was trying to correct.
notes.lesson: Never attribute a claim to the owner they did not make, and never relay an agent's finding as agreement with the owner without checking it against the owner's actual words. The audit's winner-take-all reading was presented as 'exactly as you said' when the owner had said the opposite (continuous share metric).

notes.quote: Potions are decisively powerful many times a game when humans are involved... we shouldn't prematurely discount the value of heuristics that we know advantages a Centaur team just because pure bots aren't smart enough to take advantage of those positional values
notes.lesson: Measured frequency/impact of a mechanism under our own dumb bots is endogenous, not a game fact. Centaur-valuable heuristics are not gated on pure-bot payoff.
